_note: Hand-derived from the Wikipedia Description text captured in species.raw.json. Each entry keeps the source sentence so every colour is traceable and correctable. null = the article does not state that colour; the matcher drops the trait rather than guessing. Entries past the first 100 were added later: their cap colours are palette swatches chosen by reading the quoted sentence, and species whose description gave no clear cap colour were left out (so they keep auto-extraction) rather than recorded as null.

Amanita muscaria.capSource: The bright red cap ranges from 5-30 centimetres in diameter.
Amanita muscaria.stemSource: The stipe is white, 5-20 cm high by 1-2 cm wide.

Amanita phalloides.capSource: The color of the cap can be pale-green, yellowish-green, olive-green, bronze, or (in one form) white.
Amanita phalloides.stemSource: The stipe is white with a scattering of grayish-olive scales.

Lanmaoa asiatica.capSource: It is reddish in color and an ectomycorrhizal symbiote of Pinus yunnanensis.

Psilocybe cubensis.capSource: The cap is brown becoming paler to almost white at the margin and fades to more golden-brown or yellowish with age.
Psilocybe cubensis.stemSource: The hollow white stipe is 4-15 cm high.

Agaricus bisporus.capSource: The pileus or cap of the original wild species is a pale grey-brown, with broad, flat scales on a paler background.

Psilocybe semilanceata.capSource: When it is moist, the cap is ochraceous to pale brown to dark chestnut brown, but darker in the center.
Psilocybe semilanceata.stemSource: The slender yellowish-brown stipe is 4.5-14 cm long.

Boletus edulis.capSource: The fruit body has a large brown cap which can reach 30 cm in diameter.

Coprinus comatus.capSource: The young fruit bodies first appear as white cylinders emerging from the ground, then the bell-shaped caps open out.
Coprinus comatus.stemSource: The white and fairly thick stipe measures 6-40 cm high.

Pleurotus ostreatus.capSource: In the wild, it ranges from white to gray or brown; the margin is inrolled when young.

Armillaria ostoyae.capSource: It can be distinguished from other Armillaria species by its cream-brown colors, prominent cap scales, and a well-developed ring.

Flammulina filiformis.capSource: The cap surface is smooth, viscid when damp, ochraceous yellow to yellow-brown.
Flammulina filiformis.stemSource: Pale yellow at the apex, yellow-brown to dark brown towards the base.

Chlorophyllum molybdites.capSource: The cap is whitish in colour with coarse brownish scales.

Coprinopsis atramentaria.capSource: The greyish or brownish-grey cap is furrowed, initially bell-shaped, and later more convex.
Coprinopsis atramentaria.stemSource: The stipe measures 5-17 cm high by 1-2 cm thick, is grey in colour, and lacks a ring.

Psilocybe cyanescens.capSource: A hygrophanous pileus (cap) that is caramel to chestnut-brown when moist, fading to pale buff when dried.
Psilocybe cyanescens.stemSource: The stem (which is white when undisturbed).

Psilocybe azurescens.capColorName: chestnut to ochraceous brown to caramel
Psilocybe azurescens.capSource: It is chestnut to ochraceous brown to caramel in color, often becoming pitted with dark blue or bluish black zones.

Leucocoprinus birnbaumii.capSource: The surface is lemon yellow to sulphur yellow, smooth or slightly powdery and covered in ragged, fibrous scales.

Grifola frondosa.capSource: The caps are grayish-brown, often curled or spoon-shaped, with wavy margins and 2-10 cm broad.
Grifola frondosa.stemSource: The cream-coloured stipe (stalk) has a branchy structure.

Galerina marginata.capSource: Pale to dark ochraceous tawny over the disc and yellow-ochraceous on the margin, fading to dull tan when dry.
Galerina marginata.stemSource: Below the ring it is brown down to the reddish-brown to bistre base.

Amanita caesarea.capSource: This mushroom has an orange to red cap, initially hemispherical before convex and finally flat.

Astraeus hygrometricus.capSource: The spore case is sessile, light gray to tan color and 1 to 3 cm broad; the rays are dark grey to black.

Tremella fuciformis.capSource: The fruit bodies are gelatinous, watery white, up to 7 centimetres across.

Inonotus obliquus.capSource: It is a sclerotium or mass of mycelium, mostly black because of a substantial amount of melanin.

Hydnellum peckii.capSource: The cap is initially whitish, but later turns slightly brownish, with irregular dark-brown to nearly black blotches.

Auricularia auricula-judae.capSource: The upper surface is a reddish-tan-brown with a purplish tint and finely pilose.

Pleurotus eryngii.stemSource: The whitish stem is 3-10 cm tall and 1-3 cm wide.

Agaricus campestris.capSource: The cap is white, may have fine scales, and is 3 to 12 centimetres in diameter.
Agaricus campestris.stemSource: The stipe is 3 to 10 cm tall, predominantly white and bears a single thin ring.

Cantharellus cibarius.capSource: Cantharellus cibarius is the golden chanterelle, the type species of the chanterelle genus.

Phallus impudicus.capSource: Topped with a conical cap covered with the greenish-brown slimy gleba.
Phallus impudicus.stemSource: Inside this is a white structure called the receptaculum.

Armillaria mellea.capSource: Armillaria gemina lacks the yellow cap background; the organism blooms honey mushrooms.

Coprinellus micaceus.stemSource: The stipe surface is at first velvety with a very fine whitish powder.

Amanita pantherina.capSource: Deep brown to hazel-brown to pale ochraceous brown, densely distributed warts that are pure white to sordid cream.
Amanita pantherina.stemSource: The stipe is 5-15 cm long, subcylindric, white, becoming slightly tannish in age.

Lactarius indigo.capSource: The cap surface is indigo blue when fresh, but fades to a paler grayish- or silvery-blue.

Lactarius deliciosus.capSource: Lactarius deliciosus has a carrot-orange cap that is convex to vase shaped.
Lactarius deliciosus.stemSource: It has a squat orange stipe that is often hollow, 2 to 8 cm long.

Phallus indusiatus.capSource: Its reticulated surface is covered with a layer of greenish-brown and foul-smelling slime, the gleba.
Phallus indusiatus.stemSource: The hollow stalk is white, roughly equal in width throughout its length.

Ganoderma lucidum.capSource: Reishi is a purple-brown mushroom with a long stalk, brown spores, and a fan-shaped cap with a shiny appearance.
Ganoderma lucidum.stemSource: The stipe is tawny to russet colored and 1.5 times the diameter of the cap.

Tuber melanosporum.capSource: The round, dark brown fruiting bodies have a black-brown skin with small pyramidal cusps.

Psilocybe ovoideocystidiata.capColorName: chestnut or orangish brown to pearly cream
Psilocybe ovoideocystidiata.capSource: Chestnut or orangish brown to yellowish brown to pearly cream color, hygrophanous, glabrous.
Psilocybe ovoideocystidiata.stemSource: During youth the cap is dark brown/black (the stem is white).

Cordyceps militaris.capSource: The fungus forms 1-8 centimetres high, club-shaped and orange/red fruiting bodies.

Clathrus archeri.capSource: Coated in spore-bearing gleba on the upper surface which is dark greenish-brown in colour.

Amanita virosa.capSource: It is able to be peeled and is white, though the centre may be ivory.
Amanita virosa.stemSource: The crowded, free gills are white, as is the stipe and volva.

Laetiporus sulphureus.capSource: Its fruit bodies grow as striking golden-yellow shelf-like structures on tree trunks and branches.

Panaeolus foenisecii.capColorName: brownish when moist, tannish when dry
Panaeolus foenisecii.capSource: Hygrophanous with a brownish colour when moist and tannish when dry, often with a dark band around the margin.
Panaeolus foenisecii.stemSource: The stipe is 3 to 8 cm, fragile, hollow, beige to light brown, fibrous.

Psilocybe mexicana.capColorName: ocherous to brown or beige to straw
Psilocybe mexicana.capSource: Ocherous to brown or beige to straw color in age, conic to campanulate or subumbonate.
Psilocybe mexicana.stemSource: Stipe: straw color to brownish or reddish-brown, becoming darker where injured.

Gyromitra esculenta.capSource: The cap is brownish, and can variously be shaded reddish, chestnut, purplish, or golden.
Gyromitra esculenta.stemSource: Perched on a stout white stipe up to 6 cm high.

Clathrus ruber.capSource: The dark olive-green to olive-brown, foul-smelling sticky gleba covers the inner surface of the receptacle.

Panaeolus cinctulus.capSource: Striking cinnamon-brown when moist, soot-black when wet.
Panaeolus cinctulus.stemSource: The stipe is reddish brown or covered by whitish powder, hollow.

Amanita bisporigera.capSource: The cap surface is smooth and white, sometimes with a pale tan- or cream-colored tint in the center.
Amanita bisporigera.stemSource: The white stipe is 6-14 cm by 0.7-1.8 cm thick, solid.

Omphalotus olearius.capSource: A poisonous orange gilled mushroom; Omphalotus olearius is the same shade of orange internally and externally.
Omphalotus olearius.stemSource: If the jack-o'-lantern's stem is peeled, the same shade of orange as the outer flesh.

Psilocybe tampanensis.capSource: Ochraceous brown to straw brown, buff to yellowish-grey when dry, with slight bluish tones at the margin.

Paxillus involutus.capSource: May be reddish-, yellowish- or olive-brown in colour and typically 4-12 cm wide.

Amanita ocreata.capSource: The rest of the fungus below the cap is white; occasionally parts may have pinkish tones.
Amanita ocreata.stemSource: Bearing a thin white membranous ring until old age.

Craterellus cornucopioides.capSource: The upper and inner surface is black or dark gray, and rarely yellow.

Schizophyllum commune.capSource: The caps are 1-4 centimetres wide with white or grayish hairs.

Marasmius oreades.capSource: It is dry, smooth, pale tan or buff (occasionally white), or reddish tan.

Fomes fomentarius.capSource: The upper surface is tough, bumpy, hard and woody, varying in colour, usually a light brown or grey.

Hypomyces lactifluorum.capSource: Turning them a reddish orange color; at maturity the reddish orange H. lactifluorum thoroughly covers its host.

Tuber magnatum.capSource: The flesh is pale cream or brown with white marbling.

Amanita verna.capSource: The fool's mushroom is pure white, all the way to the gills and the stipe.
Amanita verna.stemSource: The caps, stipes and gills are all white in colour.

Morchella esculenta.capSource: The cap is pale brownish cream, yellow to tan or pale brown to grayish brown.
Morchella esculenta.stemSource: The stem is white to pallid or pale yellow, hollow.

Omphalotus illudens.capSource: Desarmillaria tabescens forms small, dull orange caps.

Suillus luteus.capColorName: chestnut, rusty, olive brown or dark brown
Suillus luteus.capSource: The cap is chestnut, rusty, olive brown, or dark brown in color with a diameter of 4-10 centimetres.
Suillus luteus.stemSource: Below the ring, the stipe is dingy white, sometimes streaked with brownish slime.

Sarcoscypha coccinea.capSource: The inner surface of the cup is deep red (fading to orange when dry) and smooth.
Sarcoscypha coccinea.stemSource: The stipe is stout and up to 4 cm long, and whitish, with a tomentum.

Imleria badia.capSource: Imleria badia fruit bodies have a chestnut to dark brown cap.

Auricularia heimuer.capSource: The upper surface is finely tomentose, coloured fawn to reddish brown when fresh.

Entoloma hochstetteri.capSource: The cap colour is indigo-blue with a green tint, and is fibrillose.

Russula emetica.capSource: It is a bright scarlet or cherry red, and in maturity the margins have fine radial grooves.
Russula emetica.stemSource: The white stem measures 4.5-10.5 cm long by 0.7-2.4 cm thick.

Ganoderma applanatum.capSource: The upper surface of the fruiting body appears brown, covered with reddish-brown.

Collybia nuda.capSource: One whose gills and cap are initially light violet and mature to burgundy.

Craterellus tubaeformis.capSource: The mushroom is mostly yellow with a grayish-brown cap.
Craterellus tubaeformis.stemSource: The mushroom is mostly yellow with a grayish-brown cap.

Cerioporus squamosus.capSource: The body can be yellow to brown and has squamules or scales on its upper side.

Cortinarius violaceus.capSource: The specific epithet violaceus refers to the deep violet colour of its cap.
Cortinarius violaceus.stemSource: The stipe is a similar colour to the cap, and covered in wool-like fibrils.

Shaggy parasol.capSource: A large and conspicuous agaric, with thick brown scales and protuberances on its fleshy white cap.

Tremella mesenterica.capSource: The lobes translucent, deep yellow or bright yellow-orange, fading to pale yellow.

Hypholoma fasciculare.stemSource: The stipe is 3-12 cm tall and 3-10 mm wide, light yellow, orange-brown below.

Rubroboletus satanas.capColorName: greyish white to silvery-white or buff
Rubroboletus satanas.capSource: When young, the pileus is greyish white to silvery-white or buff.

Stropharia rugosoannulata.capSource: A reddish-brown convex to flattening cap up to 30 cm across.
Stropharia rugosoannulata.stemSource: The firm flesh is white, as is the tall stem, which bears a wrinkled ring.

Gymnopilus junonius.capSource: It is bright yellow-orange in younger specimens and orange-brown or reddish brown in older ones.

Lycoperdon perlatum.capSource: It is off-white with a top covered in short spiny bumps or jewels.
Lycoperdon perlatum.stemSource: It has a stem-like base, and is whitish before browning in age.

Coprinopsis lagopus.capColorName: pale to very dark-brown beneath a silvery grey veil
Coprinopsis lagopus.capSource: The color of the cap surface is pale to very dark-brown at center beneath the whitish to silvery grey veil.
Coprinopsis lagopus.stemSource: The stem is whitish in color, and is hollow, hairy over the whole surface.

Flammulina velutipes.capSource: The cap is light orange, darker toward the center.
Flammulina velutipes.stemSource: The flesh of the cap is yellow, while that of the stem is brown.

Aleuria aurantia.capSource: The orange fruiting body is 1-10 centimetres wide, cup-shaped, externally fuzzy.

Hygrophoropsis aurantiaca.capSource: The species has a golden-orange cap ranging from 2-10 cm in diameter.
Hygrophoropsis aurantiaca.stemSource: The orange stipe is 1.5-8 cm tall and 0.5-1 cm thick, and lacks a ring.

Hydnum repandum.capSource: The orange-, yellow- or tan-colored pileus (cap) is up to 17 centimetres wide.
Hydnum repandum.stemSource: The stipe is either white or the same color as the cap, and is sometimes off-center.

Xylaria polymorpha.capSource: The fruiting bodies can be 3-10 centimetres tall, externally colored black or brown.

Scleroderma citrinum.capSource: The fruit bodies grow to 10 centimetres broad and 6 cm high with a yellowish peridium, or outer skin.

Fomitopsis betulina.capSource: The fruit bodies are pale, with a smooth greyish-brown top surface.

Pholiota squarrosa.capSource: The cap color is yellowish-brown to tawny in older specimens.

Psilocybe caerulipes.stemSource: The stipe is 3-6 cm long, tough, and is whitish to brown at first.

Amanita jacksonii.capSource: The cap of the mushroom is 8–12 centimetres (3–4+1⁄2 inches) wide; oval at first, becoming convex, typically with a central bump; sticky; brilliant red or orange, fading to yellow on the margin; typically without warts or patches; the margin lined for about 40–50% of the cap's radius.
Amanita jacksonii.stemSource: The stipe measures 90–140 by 9–16 millimetres (3+1⁄2 in–5+1⁄2 in × 1⁄4 in–3⁄4 in), is yellow and decorated with orange fibrils and patches that are the remnants of a felted extension of the limbus internus of the otherwise white volva.

Neoboletus luridiformis.capSource: The large, solid fungus has a bay-brown hemispherical to convex cap that can grow up to 20 cm (8 in) wide and is initially velvety.
Neoboletus luridiformis.stemSource: The fat, colourful, densely red-dotted yellow stem is 4–15 cm (1+1⁄2–6 in) long and has no network pattern (reticulation).

Pleurotus citrinopileatus.capSource: The fruiting bodies grow in clusters of bright yellow to golden brown caps with a velvety, dry surface texture.
Pleurotus citrinopileatus.stemSource: The stems are cylindrical, white in color, often curved or bent, and about 2–5 cm (3⁄4–2 in) long and 2–8 mm (1⁄16–5⁄16 in) in diameter.

Psilocybe serbica.capSource: The cap is buff-brown to dingy orangish-brown and pale ochraceous when dry.

Agaricus arvensis.capSource: The cap is 7–20 cm (3–8 in) across, whitish, smooth, and dry; it stains yellow, particularly when young.

Coprinellus disseminatus.capSource: The bell-shaped cap is tannish, becoming gray with age.

Cortinarius rubellus.capSource: The mushroom is generally tan to brown all over, with a conical to convex cap 2.5 to 8 centimetres (1 to 3+1⁄4 in) in diameter, adnate gills and a 5.5 to 11 cm (2+1⁄4 to 4+1⁄4 in) tall stipe.
Cortinarius rubellus.stemSource: The mushroom is generally tan to brown all over, with a conical to convex cap 2.5 to 8 centimetres (1 to 3+1⁄4 in) in diameter, adnate gills and a 5.5 to 11 cm (2+1⁄4 to 4+1⁄4 in) tall stipe.

Psilocybe aztecorum.capColorName: dark chestnut brown to straw yellow
Psilocybe aztecorum.capSource: The color of the caps changes with variations in hydration, ranging from dark chestnut brown to straw yellow or whitish when dry.

Leccinum scabrum.capSource: The skin of the cap is tan or brownish, usually with a lighter edge; it is smooth, bald, and dry to viscid.
Leccinum scabrum.stemSource: The stipe is 5–15 cm (2–6 in) long and 1–3.5 cm (3⁄8–1+3⁄8 in) wide and slim, with white and dark to black flakes; it tapers upward.

Suillellus luridus.capSource: Suillellus luridus is a stout fungus with a thick yellow-olive to olive-brown convex cushion-shaped cap that can reach 20 cm (8 in) in diameter.
Suillellus luridus.stemSource: The stout ochre stem reaches 8–14 cm (3–6 in) high and 1–3 cm (0.4–1.2 in) wide, and is patterned with a red network.

Psilocybe allenii.capSource: The caps of the mushrooms are brown to buff, broadly convex to flattened and have a diameter up to 9 cm (3.5 in), while the white stipes are up to 9 cm (3.5 in) long and 0.7 cm (0.3 in) thick.
Psilocybe allenii.stemSource: The caps of the mushrooms are brown to buff, broadly convex to flattened and have a diameter up to 9 cm (3.5 in), while the white stipes are up to 9 cm (3.5 in) long and 0.7 cm (0.3 in) thick.

Omphalotus nidiformis.capSource: The cap is very variable in colour, sometimes cream though often tinted with orange, brownish, greyish, purple or even bluish-black shades.

Panellus stipticus.capSource: The caps are orange-yellow to brownish, and attached to the decaying wood by short stubby stalks that are connected off-center or on the side of the caps.
Panellus stipticus.stemSource: The dull-white stem is covered with minute silk-like fibers and is narrower at the base where it attaches to the substrate.

Entoloma sinuatum.capSource: The ivory to light grey-brown cap is up to 20 cm (7.9 in) across with a margin that is rolled inward.
Entoloma sinuatum.stemSource: The stout white stipe lacks a ring and is anywhere from 4 to 20 cm (1.6 to 7.9 in) high, and 0.5–4 cm (0.20–1.57 in) in diameter.

Armillaria gallica.capSource: The caps are brownish-yellow to brown when moist, often with a darker-colored center; the color tends to fade upon drying.
Armillaria gallica.stemSource: Above the level of the ring, the stem is pale orange to brown, while below it is whitish or pale pink, becoming grayish-brown at the base.

Hypsizygus tessulatus.capSource: The white to yellow cap is 5–15 centimetres (2–6 in) across, convex then flat and sunken.

Panaeolus papilionaceus.capSource: The cap is 1–5 centimetres (1⁄2–2 in) across, obtusely conic then becoming campanulate, and grayish brown.
Panaeolus papilionaceus.stemSource: The stipe is 6–12 cm by 2–4 mm, gray-brown to reddish brown, darker where handled, paler toward the apex, brittle, fibrous, and pruinose.

Meripilus giganteus.capColorName: pale tan to dull chestnut brown
Meripilus giganteus.capSource: The color of the cap surface is pale tan to dull chestnut brown in young specimens but darkens in age to become concentric zones (zonate) of various shades of brown.

Phallus rubicundus.capSource: The wrinkled cap is scarlet red, and measures 2–3 cm (0.8–1.2 in) high by 1–2 cm (0.4–0.8 in) wide.
Phallus rubicundus.stemSource: The orange to scarlet stalk tapers towards to top, and has a pitted surface.

Volvopluteus gloiocephalus.capSource: The cap of the mushroom is about 5–15 cm (2–6 in) in diameter, varies from white to grey or grey-brown, and is markedly sticky when fresh.
Volvopluteus gloiocephalus.stemSource: The stipe is white and has a sack-like volva at the base.

Amanita citrina.capSource: This mushroom has a fleshy pale yellow, or sometimes white, cap from 4–10 centimetres (1+1⁄2–4 inches) across, covered in irregular patches.
Amanita citrina.stemSource: It bears a pale yellow or sometimes white cap, with white stem, ring and volva.

Mycena subcyanocephala.capColorName: white with a pale blue tone
Mycena subcyanocephala.capSource: It is currently the smallest known mushroom in the world, with caps about 1 mm tall and a white color with a pale blue tone.

Pleurocybella porrigens.capSource: The mushroom species is distinguished by its fruit bodies, pure white when young and sometimes yellowing with age.

Candy cap.capSource: Candy caps are small to medium-size mushrooms, with a pileus ranging from 2–7 centimetres (3⁄4–2+3⁄4 in) in diameter, and colored orange-brown to reddish-brown.

Baorangia bicolor.capSource: The color of the cap is light red when young and brick red in maturity.
Baorangia bicolor.stemSource: The stem coloration is yellow at the apex and a red or rosy red for the lower two thirds.

Agaricus subrufescens.capColorName: white to grayish or dull reddish brown
Agaricus subrufescens.capSource: The color of the cap may range from white to grayish or dull reddish brown; it stains yellow in KOH.

Pluteus cervinus.capColorName: deer-brown, light ochre-brown to dark brown
Pluteus cervinus.capSource: The cap can be deer-brown, but varies from light ochre-brown to dark brown, with a variable admixture of grey or black.

Clitocybe nebularis.capSource: Cap colours are generally greyish to light brownish-grey, and often covered in a whitish bloom when young.

Clitocybe dealbata.capSource: A small white or white dusted with buff-coloured mushroom, the 2–4 cm diameter cap is flattened to depressed with adnate to decurrent crowded white gills.

Ramaria stricta.capSource: The color of the fruit body is brownish to yellow, becoming paler toward extremities.

Amanita vaginata.capSource: The cap is 3 to 10 centimetres (1 to 4 inches) in diameter and gray to grayish-brown in color; initially the cap is oval, then as it matures it becomes progressively conical, convex, and eventually flattened, sometimes with a small umbo (a rounded elevation in the center of the cap).

Tylopilus felleus.capSource: The fruit bodies have convex to flat caps that are some shade of brown, buff or tan and typically measure up to 15 cm (6 in) in diameter.

Leratiomyces ceres.capSource: Cap: 2 to 6 cm in diameter, with thin flesh and a bright red to orange top which is convex to plane in age.
Leratiomyces ceres.stemSource: Stipe: Whitish, often with dark orange stains in age (most evident around base), 3–6 cm long and 0.5 to 1 cm wide, equal to slightly larger at the base, which often has mycelium attached.

Mycena interrupta.capSource: The caps of Mycena interrupta range from 0.8 to 2 cm, and are a brilliant cyan blue colour.
Mycena interrupta.stemSource: It is white and smooth, and the base of the stipe is attached to the wood substrate by a flat white disk, similar to Roridomyces austrororidus which, unlike M.

Calocybe gambosa.capSource: The colour of the cap, stipe and flesh ranges from white to creamy.
Calocybe gambosa.stemSource: The colour of the cap, stipe and flesh ranges from white to creamy.

Suillus granulatus.capSource: The orange-brown, to brown-yellow cap is viscid (sticky) when wet, and shiny when dry, and is usually 4 to 12 centimetres (1+1⁄2 to 4+3⁄4 in) in diameter.
Suillus granulatus.stemSource: The pale yellow stem is about 4–8 cm (1+1⁄2–3+1⁄4 in) tall  1–2 cm (3⁄8–3⁄4 in) wide, and of uniform thickness; it has tiny brownish granules at the apex and lacks a ring.

Agaricus augustus.capColorName: brown scales on a white to yellow background
Agaricus augustus.capSource: The cap cuticle is dry, and densely covered with concentrically arranged, brown-coloured scales on a white to yellow background.
Agaricus augustus.stemSource: Above the ring, the stem is white to yellow and smooth.

Mycena chlorophos.capSource: Fruit bodies (mushrooms) have pale brownish-grey sticky caps up to 30 mm (1.2 in) in diameter atop stems 6–30 mm (0.2–1.2 in) long and up to a millimeter thick.
Mycena chlorophos.stemSource: The white stem is 6–30 mm (0.24–1.18 in) long by 0.3–1 mm thick, hollow, and translucent.

Cortinarius iodes.capSource: The fruit bodies have small, slimy caps which are up to 6 cm (2+1⁄4 in) in diameter and purple, developing yellowish spots and streaks in maturity.
Cortinarius iodes.stemSource: It is solid (i.e., not hollow), slimy, smooth, and has violet or purplish colors that are usually lighter than the cap; sometimes, the stem base is more or less white.

Psilocybe pelliculosa.capSource: The fruit bodies, or mushrooms, have a conical brownish cap up to 2 cm (3⁄4 in) in diameter atop a slender stem up to 8 cm (3+1⁄8 in) long.
Psilocybe pelliculosa.stemSource: The lower region of the stem is brownish in color and has silky fibrils pressed against the stem; the upper region is grayish and pruinose (lightly dusted with powdery white granules).

Tricholoma equestre.capSource: The cap ranges from 5–15 centimetres (2–6 in) in width and is usually yellow with brownish areas, particularly at the centre.
Tricholoma equestre.stemSource: The yellow stem is 4–10 cm long and 1–2 cm wide, and brownish at the base.

Lactarius deterrimus.capSource: The cap is tangerine to orange-brown, darker zoned towards the edges and dulls mainly yellow-brown.
Lactarius deterrimus.stemSource: The mainly long and cylindrical stipe is reddish orange.

Xerocomellus chrysenteron.capSource: When fully expanded, the brownish cap ranges from 4 to 10 cm (1+1⁄2 to 4 in) in diameter with very little substance and thin flesh that turns a blue color when slightly cut or bruised.
Xerocomellus chrysenteron.stemSource: The 1 to 2 cm-diameter stems have no ring, are mostly bright yellow and the lower part is covered in coral-red fibrils and has a constant elliptical to fusiform diameter throughout its length of 4 to 13 cm.

Phellinus ellipsoideus.capSource: Found in China, the fruit bodies produced by the species are brown, woody basidiocarps that grow on dead wood, where the fungus feeds as a saprotroph.

Leccinum aurantiacum.capSource: The cap is orange-red and measures 5–15 centimetres (2–6 inches) across.

Sarcodon imbricatus.capColorName: brownish or buff with darker scales
Sarcodon imbricatus.capSource: The brownish or buff cap measures up to 15 centimetres (6 in) in diameter and is covered with coarse darker brown scales, becoming darker and upturned with age.
Sarcodon imbricatus.stemSource: The pale grey or brown stipe may reach 10 cm (4 in) high and 4 cm (1+1⁄2 in) wide, may be narrower at the base, and is sometimes eccentric.

Suillus americanus.capSource: The cap surface is colored bright yellow with red or brownish streaks and hairy patches.
Suillus americanus.stemSource: The color of the stipe surface is lemon yellow, and it is covered with glandular dots that bruise if handled.

Amanita flavoconia.capSource: It has an orangish-yellow cap with yellowish-orange patches or warts, a yellowish-orange annulus, and a white to orange stem.
Amanita flavoconia.stemSource: It has an orangish-yellow cap with yellowish-orange patches or warts, a yellowish-orange annulus, and a white to orange stem.

Mycena haematopus.capSource: They are characterized by their reddish color, the scalloped cap edges, and the dark red latex they "bleed" when cut or broken.
Mycena haematopus.stemSource: The stem is 3–9 cm (1+1⁄8–3+1⁄2 in) tall and 0.1–0.2 cm (1⁄32–3⁄32 in) thick, hollow and brittle, and a dark reddish-brown color.

Suillus bovinus.capSource: The mushroom has a convex grey-yellow or ochre cap reaching up to 10 cm (4 in) in diameter, which flattens with age.
Suillus bovinus.stemSource: The stipe is 4–6 cm (1+1⁄2–2+1⁄4 in) tall, similar in colour to the cap, and tends to be narrower towards the base.

Russula brevipes.capSource: Fully grown, the cap can range from 7 to 30 cm (3 to 12 in) in diameter, whitish to dull-yellow, and is funnel-shaped with a central depression.
Russula brevipes.stemSource: The fruit bodies are white and large, with convex to funnel-shaped caps measuring 7–30 cm (3–12 in) wide set atop a thick stipe up to 8 cm (3 in) long.

Boletus pinophilus.capSource: It has a red-brown to maroon-coloured cap and a large and bulbous stipe, covered with coarse orange-red reticulation.

Mycena galericulata.capSource: The cap's color varies from grayish brown to dark brown and the shape ranges from bell-like to bluntly conical to flattened with an umbo.
Mycena galericulata.stemSource: The stem color is pale grayish white on the upper portion, and pale grayish black below; the base becomes somewhat dirty brown in age, but does not develop reddish stains.

Verpa bohemica.capSource: The cap varies in color from yellowish brown to reddish brown, with a pale underside, is attached to the stem at the top only, with the lobed edge free.
Verpa bohemica.stemSource: The stem is 6 to 12 cm (2+3⁄8 to 4+3⁄4 in) long and 1 to 2.5 cm (3⁄8 to 1 in) thick, cream-white in color, and tapering upward.

Panaeolus olivaceus.capSource: Cap: 1 — 4 cm across, Distinctly campanulate then subhemispheric to convex, becoming broadly conic, not fully expanding, incurved margin when young, dark smoky-grayish to dark cinnamon, drying to a straw-yellow or slightly olive-gray color, remaining more reddish-brown towards the center, hygrophanous, smooth, sometimes striated or finely corrugated, flesh thick and firm.

Strobilomyces strobilaceus.capSource: The cap surface is covered with tuft-like, dark grey to brown erect scales.
Strobilomyces strobilaceus.stemSource: It is coloured like the cap and has a woolly surface and a thick, ascending annulus or merely bands of colour from the partial veil.

Candolleomyces candolleanus.capSource: The cap is tan when young, fading to whitish, and growing to 2–8 cm (1–3 in) in diameter; they are initially conical, later becoming rounded and finally with upturned margins in maturity.
Candolleomyces candolleanus.stemSource: The white stalk is 4–10 cm (1.5–4 in) tall and 3–7 mm wide.

Gymnopilus luteofolius.capSource: The fruit bodies have reddish to purplish to yellow caps 2 to 11 centimetres (3⁄4 to 4+1⁄4 in) in diameter, which can stain bluish-green.
Gymnopilus luteofolius.stemSource: The stipe is the same color as the cap, often dusted with rusty-brown spores, fibrillose, measuring 3–9 by 3–10 mm thick, equal to enlarged near the base.

Turbinellus floccosus.capSource: Colored various shades of reddish- to yellowish-orange, the cap surface is broken into scales, with the spaces between more yellow and the scales themselves more orange.

Hygrocybe conica.capSource: The cap surface is smooth and finely fibrillose, moist or viscid at first, variously yellow to orange or scarlet.
Hygrocybe conica.stemSource: The stipe (stem) is up to 20 cm (8 in) long, smooth but fibrillose and streaky, yellow to orange-red, whitish towards base, lacking a ring.

Gliophorus psittacinus.capSource: The parrot toadstool is a small mushroom, with a convex to umbonate cap up to 4 centimetres (1.6 in) in diameter, which is green when young and later yellowish or even pinkish tinged.
Gliophorus psittacinus.stemSource: The stipe, measuring 2–8 cm (0.8–3.1 in) in length and 3–5 mm in width, is green to greenish yellow.

Lactarius torminosus.capSource: A blend of pink and ochre hues, the cap sometimes has concentric zones of alternating lighter and darker shades.
Lactarius torminosus.stemSource: The cylindrical stem is a pale flesh color with a delicately downy surface and brittle flesh; it is up to 8 cm (3 in) long and 0.6–2 cm (1⁄4–3⁄4 in) thick.

Leucocoprinus leucothites.capSource: The mushroom's cap is 4 to 15 centimetres (1+1⁄2 to 6 in) wide, is granular, white or gray-brown in color then sometimes grayish or pinkish.

Psilocybe atlantis.capSource: The cap surface is pale brown to reddish brown in color, hygrophanous, and bruises blue where damaged.

Hortiboletus rubellus.capSource: This cap is scarlet to raspberry red when young, with a dry velvety texture, often cracking in age.
Hortiboletus rubellus.stemSource: Hortiboletus rubellus, commonly known as the ruby bolete, is a small, dainty, brightly coloured member of the family Boletaceae, with a reddish cap and stipe, and yellow pores.

Psathyrella aquatica.capSource: Its cap is brown, convex, and has gills underneath.

Amanita gemmata.capSource: The fruit body has a cap that is a dull to golden shade of yellow, and typically 2.5–12 centimetres (1–4+3⁄4 inches) in diameter.
Amanita gemmata.stemSource: The stem is pale yellow, and measures 4–12 cm (1+5⁄8–4+3⁄4 in) long by 0.5–1.9 cm (1⁄4–3⁄4 in) thick.

Panaeolus antillarum.capColorName: white to light gray or yellowish
Panaeolus antillarum.capSource: Cap: 3 to 6 cm, bell-shaped to convex, white to light gray or yellowish.

Amanita regalis.capSource: regalis has a scabby liver-brown cap and a stem which is yellow-ochre at the base, with patches or rings of patches.
Amanita regalis.stemSource: A. regalis has a scabby liver-brown cap and a stem which is yellow-ochre at the base, with patches or rings of patches.

Lepiota brunneoincarnata.capSource: The mushroom has a brown scaled cap up to 4 cm wide with a pinkish brown stem and white gills.
Lepiota brunneoincarnata.stemSource: The upper part of the stem is pinkish tan while the lower part is covered in dark brown scales.

Infundibulicybe geotropa.capSource: A cream- or buff-coloured mushroom, the cap may reach 20 cm (8 in) in diameter.

Stropharia caerulea.capSource: The fruit bodies (mushrooms) of Stropharia caerulea feature a greenish-blue cap sparsely covered in white flecks of veil at the margin, and a sticky, glutinous surface texture.
Stropharia caerulea.stemSource: The greenish stipe is covered in white scales up to a thin, transient ring.

Aspropaxillus giganteus.capSource: It has a white or pale cream cap, and is funnel-shaped when mature, with the gills running down the length of the stem.
Aspropaxillus giganteus.stemSource: The stem is off-white with reddish-brown fibers and has dimensions, when mature, of 3 to 10 cm (1.2 to 3.9 in) tall and 2 to 5 cm (0.8 to 2.0 in) thick.

Clitocybe rivulosa.capSource: A small whitish mushroom, the 3–4 cm diameter cap is funnel-shaped with decurrent crowded white gills, with specks of pink.

Xylaria hypoxylon.capSource: The fruit bodies, characterized by erect, elongated black branches with whitened tips, typically grow in clusters on decaying hardwood.

Russula virescens.capSource: It can be recognized by its distinctive pale green cap that measures up to 15 cm (6 in) in diameter, the surface of which is covered with darker green angular patches.
Russula virescens.stemSource: The stipe is cylindrical, white, and of variable height, up to 8 cm (3 in) tall and 4 cm (1.6 in) wide; it is roughly the same thickness at both the top and the base.

Hebeloma aminophilum.capSource: The dull pinkish brown or cream cap is 3–11 centimetres (1–4+1⁄2 inches) in diameter, convex initially before flattening out with age.

Helvella crispa.capSource: The mushroom is readily identified by its irregularly shaped whitish cap, fluted stem, and fuzzy undersurfaces.
Helvella crispa.stemSource: The stem is 3–10 cm (1¼–4 in) long, white or pinkish in colour and ornately ribbed.

Chlorociboria aeruginascens.capSource: Chlorociboria aeruginascens is a saprobic species of mushroom, commonly known as the blue stain, green elfcup or the green wood cup because of its characteristic small, green, saucer-shaped fruit bodies.

Russula xerampelina.capSource: The colour is variable, most commonly purple to wine-red, or greenish, and darker towards the centre of the cap.
Russula xerampelina.stemSource: The stipe is 4–12 cm (1.5–4.5 in) long, 1.5–4 cm (0.5–1.5 in) wide, cylindrical, white or sometimes with a reddish blush, bruising brown.

Cortinarius caperatus.capSource: caperatus has a buff to brownish-ochre cap 5–12 centimetres (2–4+3⁄4 in) diameter, which is covered with whitish fibres.
Cortinarius caperatus.stemSource: The stipe is 4–12 cm (1+1⁄2–4+3⁄4 in) long and 1–2.2 cm (1⁄2–3⁄4 in) thick; it is slightly swollen at the base, and whitish to beige with a noteworthy whitish ring, which is initially attached to the cap.

Clavaria fragilis.capSource: The fruit bodies of are irregularly tubular, smooth to furrowed, sometimes compressed, very fragile, white, and up to 15 cm (6 in) tall by 7 mm (1⁄4 in) thick.

Agrocybe praecox.capSource: The cap is up to 10 centimeters (4 inches) wide, bun-shaped and brownish then convex and lightening to tannish (beige when dry and yellowish-brown when moist), and smooth.

Leucocoprinus cepistipes.capSource: Bulbous when immature becoming convex with a pronounced umbo which may be darker in the centre against the white colour of the rest of the cap.
Leucocoprinus cepistipes.stemSource: He noted the thin and smooth stem white stem with 'very numerous droplets of an aqueous silver, as if it were sprinkled with dew'.

Helvella lacunosa.capSource: It has an irregularly folded or wrinkled cap which may be shades of slatey grey to black, and measure anywhere from 1 to 10 centimetres (1⁄2 to 4 inches), though usually between 2 and 5 cm (1 and 2 in).
Helvella lacunosa.stemSource: The stem may be white when young and darker with age, though may be any shade of grey.

Psilocybe makarorae.capSource: The fruit body (mushroom) has a brownish cap with lighter coloured margins, measuring up to 3.5 cm (1.4 in) wide.
Psilocybe makarorae.stemSource: The whitish stipe is 30–60 millimetres (1.2–2.4 in) long by 2–4 mm wide.

Xerocomus subtomentosus.capSource: The pale olive or tan cap is initially convex before flattening and measures 4 to 10 cm (1+1⁄2 to 4 in), exceptionally up to 20 cm (7+3⁄4 in) in diameter.

Gyroporus cyanescens.capSource: The yellowish to buff cap surface is fibrous and roughened, and reaches up to 12 cm (4.7 in) in diameter.
Gyroporus cyanescens.stemSource: Roughly the same color as the cap or lighter, the stem surface is dry and lacks reticulations.

Bolbitius titubans.capColorName: yellow or bright yellow, fading with age
Bolbitius titubans.capSource: The cap's color starts yellow or bright yellow, and fades to whitish or greyish with age.
Bolbitius titubans.stemSource: The stem is 3–12 cm (1–4+1⁄2 in) tall and 2–6 millimetres (1⁄8–1⁄4 in) wide, whitish-yellow with a fine mealy powdering, and very delicate.

Clavaria zollingeri.capSource: It produces striking tubular, purple to pinkish-violet fruit bodies that grow up to 10 cm (4 in) tall and 7 cm (2+3⁄4 in) wide.

Suillus grevillei.capSource: Suillus grevillei is a mushroom with a 5–10 cm (2–4 in) cap colored from citrus yellow to burnt orange, that is at first hemispherical, then bell-shaped, and finally flattened.

Tricholoma terreum.capSource: The cap is 4–7 centimetres (1+1⁄2–2+3⁄4 inches) wide and evenly covered in fine grey scales.
Tricholoma terreum.stemSource: The whitish stipe is 3–8 cm (1+1⁄4–3+1⁄4 in) long and 1.5 cm (1⁄2 in) wide and has no ring.

Psilocybe stuntzii.capColorName: olive-greenish fading to pale yellowish brown
Psilocybe stuntzii.capSource: The pileus is olive-greenish at times, fading to a pale yellowish brown or pale yellow.

Deconica coprophila.capSource: The hemispherical cap is up to 2.5 centimetres (1 in) wide, red then orangish, usually with a hygrophanous central blotch.

Boletus aereus.capSource: The fruit body has a large dark brown cap, which can reach 30 cm (12 in) in diameter.
Boletus aereus.stemSource: The squat brown stipe, or stem, is up to 15 cm (6 in) tall and 10 cm (4 in) thick and partially covered with a raised network pattern, or reticulation.

Amanita smithiana.capSource: The cap has a diameter of 5–17 centimetres (2–6+1⁄2 inches) and is white and scaled with remnants of the universal veil.
Amanita smithiana.stemSource: The stipe is 6–18 cm (2+1⁄2–7 in) long by 1–3.5 cm (1⁄2–1+1⁄2 in) thick, white and similarly scaled, with a ring.

Volvariella bombycina.capSource: The cap, which can attain a diameter of up to 20 centimetres (8 inches), is white to slightly yellowish and covered with silky hairs.

Calocera viscosa.capSource: Calocera viscosa forms bright golden to orange-yellow (rarely white), firmly gelatinous fruit bodies up to 10 centimetres (4 in) tall, with a paler stem and coral-like branches.

Pholiota aurivella.capSource: The cap is up to 16 centimetres (6+1⁄4 in) wide, bright to golden yellow, viscid when young and with relatively dark scales.

Lactifluus piperatus.capSource: The cap is 6–16 centimetres (2+1⁄4–6+1⁄4 in) across, convex, and depressed in the center; it is creamy-white (staining tannish in age), glabrous but not glossy; it may crack in dry areas.
Lactifluus piperatus.stemSource: The stipe is white in colour, smooth, 2–8 cm (1–3 in) long and 1–3 cm (1⁄2–1+1⁄4 in) thick, and cylindrical, sometimes tapering towards the base.

Lacrymaria lacrymabunda.capSource: The yellowish to grayish cap is up to 8 centimetres (3+1⁄4 in) wide, and sometimes orangish in the center.

Hygrocybe coccinea.capSource: A small waxcap with an initially bell-shaped, and later flattening, cap 2–5 centimetres (3⁄4–2 in) across, scarlet in colour and slimy in texture.
Hygrocybe coccinea.stemSource: The ringless stipe is 2–5 cm tall and 0.3–1 cm (1⁄8–3⁄8 in) wide, red with a yellowish base.

Ileodictyon cibarium.capSource: The developing fruiting bodies (basidiocarps), or "eggs", are white, nearly globe-shaped to obovate, and up to 7 cm (2.8 in) in diameter.

Saproamanita thiersii.capSource: The cap is white and dry, measuring 3.5–10 centimetres (1+1⁄2–4 inches) wide, and convex in shape (conico- or plano-convex).
Saproamanita thiersii.stemSource: The stipe is white and is 8–20 cm (3–8 in) long and 10–20 mm (1⁄2–3⁄4 in) wide.

Leucocoprinus cretaceus.capColorName: white, brownish yellow at the centre
Leucocoprinus cretaceus.capSource: The surface is white and covered with woolly warts and scales (floccose squamulose) with a brownish yellow tinge at the centre of the cap.

Cantharellus formosus.capColorName: orange yellow to light yellow brown
Cantharellus formosus.capSource: In dry weather, the cap is medium orange yellow to light yellow brown, but wet weather may brighten the cap to brilliant to soft orange yellow.
Cantharellus formosus.stemSource: The stem is colored similarly to the cap, and is either equal-width or tapering downwards.

Cortinarius orellanus.capSource: In colour, it is an orange-brown, and is covered in fine, fibrous scales but becomes smooth with age.
